name: How are transitions handled between kitchen flooring and adjacent living areas?

mainEntity.name: How are transitions handled between kitchen flooring and adjacent living areas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Transitions between the kitchen and adjacent rooms must account for height differences and movement gaps. When moving from thick tile to lower carpet or hardwood, installers use sloped threshold reducers or custom wood transition strips to eliminate tripping hazards and ensure a smooth visual break. For open-concept floor plans popular in modern Colorado homes, many homeowners choose to run continuous luxury vinyl plank or hardwood across both the kitchen and living room to create a unified, expansive aesthetic without any transition strips at all.
acceptedAnswer.description: Installers use sloped reducers or threshold strips to bridge height differences smoothly, or run continuous flooring across open layouts to eliminate transitions entirely.
